title: transport_viz --json output (schema_version 1)
description: Minimal contract that front-ends rely on. Unknown keys are allowed so the tool can add fields without a schema bump; a breaking change bumps schema_version.

participants.description: every discovered participant with the inputs of the SHM split verdicts (#125): its SHM ports, what their lock files say in the tool's /dev/shm and how many participants announce each number; absent when nothing was discovered

reason_code_remedies.description: What to change to get past each code of reason_code_descriptions (same keys); null when the code describes a normal state or asks for a bug report.

selectedLocator.description: The reader locator the prediction selected: the address, or for SHM the /dev/shm port, the writer will deliver to. null when none was selected: a DATA_SHARING or NONE verdict, or Fast DDS < 2.10 hiding a same-host peer's locators.

measuredLocator.description: One destination locator that carried packets to the reader. packets/bytes are deltas over the observation, so the entries sum to measurement.packets/bytes.

buffer_parent_guid.description: rmw_fastrtps_cpp native-buffer companion (<topic>/_buf_cpu): the guid of the writer or reader of the parent topic whose samples it carries; absent for other endpoints

partitions.description: partition names; empty = the default partition

datasharing_history_bytes.description: size of the writer's data-sharing history file in the tool's /dev/shm; null when there is none

datasharing_segment_visibility.description: whether this endpoint's data-sharing segment (a writer's history, a reader's notification file) is in the tool's /dev/shm; probed only for an endpoint on the tool's host whose QoS announces data-sharing (ON or AUTO), unprobed otherwise and in documents before #163

packets.description: RTPS packets to the reader's locators during the observation

bytes.description: RTPS bytes to the reader's locators during the observation

delivered_samples.description: HISTORY_LATENCY samples seen for this pair during the observation

delivered_per_s.description: delivered samples per second (#143): HISTORY_LATENCY samples of this pair inside delivered_per_s_window_s, (n - 1) over the span of their source timestamps; null below two samples or without --stats

delivered_per_s_lower_bound.description: the statistics writer of the reader's participant skipped sequence numbers inside the window: delivered_per_s is at least the value, and the tool cannot say which of that participant's pairs lost

delivered_per_s_window_s.description: seconds the rate was measured over: the whole observation (observation_seconds) one-shot, the last kStatsRateWindowSeconds (5) under --watch

data_submessages.description: DATA/DATA_FRAG submessages the writer sent through a transport during the observation (DATA_COUNT delta); null when the writer's participant does not publish DATA_COUNT

packets_total.description: RTPS packets to the reader's locators since the writer's participant started

bytes_total.description: RTPS bytes to the reader's locators since the writer's participant started

throughput_bytes_per_s.description: removed in #137 and always null: PUBLICATION_THROUGHPUT is a per-write payload/interval sample, not a rate, and is no longer subscribed. The key is kept so earlier documents keep validating.

latency_s.description: HISTORY_LATENCY of this pair over the observation, seconds; null without values

reliability.description: reliability counters over the observation (window deltas); null without counters

lost_packets.description: RTPS_LOST packets the reader's participant missed from the writer's participant on the reader's unicast locators (shared by every pair of the two participants); null when the reader's participant does not publish RTPS_LOST

throughput_bytes_per_s.description: removed in #137 and always null; see the pair-level key of the same name

latency_s.description: mean write-to-notification latency of the slowest pair (HISTORY_LATENCY, seconds); null without values

lost_packets.description: RTPS_LOST packets of the pairs during the observation, each stats.lost entry counted once; null when no pair has it

resent_datas.description: sum of the pairs' RESENT_DATAS during the observation; null without counters

participants_with_stats.description: GUID prefixes of the participants that published a statistics sample the tool received (not those only named in one). Output of earlier versions can also list the participants named in a sample, the tool's own among them (#113).

packets_first.description: cumulative RTPS_SENT packets at the first sample of the observation

bytes_first.description: cumulative RTPS_SENT bytes at the first sample of the observation

data_count.description: writer guid -> cumulative DATA_COUNT at the first and last sample seen

throughput.description: removed in #137 and always empty: PUBLICATION_THROUGHPUT is no longer subscribed

samples_lost.description: statistics samples that never reached the tool because the writers' keep-last history overwrote them before it read them (#134): a pair can show no measurement although it carries traffic. Cumulative over the run. Not to be confused with `lost` above, which is what the observed system lost (RTPS_LOST).

samples_lost_at_start.description: statistics samples lost while the writers were still matching the tool's readers (#134): everything a writer's history had already dropped before the match is reported to the new reader. Normal, and excluded from the stats-samples-lost warning.

samples_rejected.description: statistics samples a resource limit of the tool's readers refused (#134); counted with samples_lost for the warning

samples_lost_latency.description: the part of samples_lost that HISTORY_LATENCY's reader reported (#141). That reader is best-effort by design, so it sees every sequence gap; the samples it misses coarsen the LATENCY of a pair instead of costing its measurement, and they raise no stats-samples-lost warning. Optional; documents written before #141 do not carry it.

writers_incompatible_qos.description: statistics DataWriters the tool's readers could not match because the writers' QoS is incompatible with theirs (#141). Nothing such a writer publishes ever arrives, and nothing is counted in samples_lost either: a reader is only told about the samples of writers it did match. Optional; documents written before #141 do not carry it.

writers_announced.description: statistics RTPS_SENT writers (one per participant with statistics) the tool's reader matched (#168). What the settle rule of a --stats one-shot waits to hear from: RTPS_SENT is what `measured` means, and every participant sends something within seconds, while the event counters (RTPS_LOST, GAP_COUNT, ...) stay silent on a healthy system. Optional; documents written before #168 do not carry it.

writers_heard.description: those of writers_announced a sample was taken from (#168): a writer's transient-local history arrives as one handoff, so its first sample says the handoff has begun. Optional; documents written before #168 do not carry it.

settled.description: whether the --stats one-shot ended because discovery was quiet for --quiet seconds, at least 5 s had passed and writers_heard reached writers_announced (#168), which is what discovery.stopped_on = settled says as well. false under --watch and when --timeout was hit first. Optional; documents written before #168 do not carry it.

settled_at_s.description: seconds after the start at which the run settled (#168); null when it did not (--timeout first, or --watch). Optional; documents written before #168 do not carry it.

pairs_delivered.description: pairs of this document whose delivery HISTORY_LATENCY proves (#147). Data-sharing pairs (no RTPS trace by design), pairs that should carry nothing (qos-incompatible, shm-ipc-namespace-split) and stats-writer-instance-limit-suspected pairs are left out. Optional; documents written before #147 do not carry it.

pairs_delivered_unmeasured.description: the pairs_delivered that RTPS_SENT shows no packet for during the observation: the lost measurements (#147). Only a delivery proof tells a pair whose RTPS_SENT samples did not arrive from an idle one. stats-samples-lost is raised only when this is above 0 and counter samples were lost or rejected. Optional; documents written before #147 do not carry it.

pairs_delivered_absent.description: the pairs_delivered_unmeasured that no lost statistics sample explains (#152): no RTPS_SENT instance was seen for the pair at all, or no counter sample was lost. Above 0 it raises rtps-sent-absent (on Fast DDS 3.6 the statistics writers stall between periodic heartbeats); stats-samples-lost counts only the remaining unmeasured pairs. Optional; documents written before #152 do not carry it.

warnings.description: document-level warning codes about the statistics observation: stats-samples-lost, rtps-sent-absent

statistics_writers.description: statistics DataWriters seen in discovery (participant prefix, topic)

lost.description: RTPS_LOST: packets the reporting participant missed from a sending participant, per the reporter's own locator the sender addressed (cumulative, with the first sample of the observation)

reporter_participant_guid_prefix.description: the receiving participant that published the sample

pairKey.description: Identity of a writer -> reader pair: the display topic name and the two endpoint GUIDs, with the nodes behind them (empty for an endpoint without a ROS node).

changes.description: Pairs added, removed or changed between two snapshots. In --watch --json documents: since the previously emitted document (empty in the first one), pairs matched by GUID. In the output of `transport_viz diff --json`: between the before document (`before`) and this one, matched by `key`; the keys of added_pairs and changed_pairs are this document's, those of removed_pairs the before document's, and changed_pairs[].from names the pair's GUIDs in the before document.

key.description: How the pairs of the two snapshots were matched: by (topic, writer GUID, reader GUID) or by (topic, writer node, reader node), which survives a restart of the nodes and ignores the locator port numbers a restart renumbers (`diff --key node`, the default of diff).

before.description: The before document of `transport_viz diff` (absent in --watch output).

allOf.description: The state of the pair in the before document, with the GUIDs it had there (they differ from the key's after a restart of the nodes, under `key` = node).

discovery.description: how complete the observation behind this document is - a property of the observation, not of the observed system; absent in documents written before this field existed

complete.description: true when every endpoint the live participants announce in ros_discovery_info was discovered, false when some were missed (the run stopped too early), null when no live participant announced anything and nothing can be said either way

stopped_on.description: what ended the observation: a --quiet window without discovery events, --timeout, or (with --stats, #168) that window once every matched statistics RTPS_SENT writer was heard from

endpoints.description: remote endpoints discovered, before any view filter (--all, --topic, --node)

announced_not_discovered.description: endpoints announced by a live participant that discovery never delivered; 0 when complete is true

observer_protocol.description: how the tool's own participants took part in discovery (#86): CLIENT or SUPER_CLIENT under ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER (SUPER_CLIENT unless ROS_SUPER_CLIENT says otherwise), SUPER_CLIENT under ROS2_EASY_MODE, SIMPLE otherwise; absent in documents written before this field existed

discovery_servers.description: the servers ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER names, parsed as Fast DDS does (default port 11811, a number below 420 read as a domain id, host names resolved); empty without the variable

discovery_server_env.description: ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER as set, empty without it

easy_mode.description: ROS2_EASY_MODE as set (the address of this host's auto-started Discovery Server), empty without it

shm.description: shared memory of the environment the tool runs in (statvfs of /dev/shm and the Fast DDS files in it); the sizes are absent when `available` is false

fastdds_bytes.description: sum of the fastrtps_* / fast_datasharing_* file sizes

datasharing_notifications.description: notification segments (fast_datasharing_<reader guid>) of discovered data-sharing readers, not counted in datasharing_histories

nodes_visible.description: no missing port and no participant with another host id: the observed nodes share this /dev/shm

checked_ports.description: SHM ports of observed nodes on the tool's host id that were probed here

missing_ports.description: probed ports not held by a living process here (or the tool's own port number)

unknown_ports.description: of the missing ports, those whose lock is free or could not be probed: they leave the participant unprobed instead of not visible

other_host_participants.description: observed participants with another host id: never in this /dev/shm

participant.description: a discovered participant; endpoints name it by participant_guid_prefix

host_id.description: first 4 bytes of the GUID prefix, hex

host.description: host label as on the endpoints

own.description: one of the tool's own participants

discovery_protocol.description: the PARTICIPANT_TYPE the participant announced, verbatim (#86): SIMPLE, CLIENT, SUPER_CLIENT, SERVER or BACKUP; empty when it announced none (a non-Fast DDS vendor, the tool's own participants). Fast DDS 3.6 announces a CLIENT as SUPER_CLIENT

name.description: the participant name it announced (a ROS 2 node's is its enclave, "/"; the Easy Mode server is DiscoveryServerAuto)

vendor.description: "eProsima" or the vendor id as two hex bytes "xx.xx"

metatraffic_locators.description: its metatraffic unicast locators: where a Discovery Server listens, where a client is reached by discovery

discovery_server.description: guid_prefix of the Discovery Server this participant is a client of, when that is certain: exactly one SERVER was discovered, or under Easy Mode the DiscoveryServerAuto of the participant's host; null otherwise (a client's own server list is not on the wire), and for servers, SIMPLE participants and the tool's own

shm_visibility.description: whether the participant listens for SHM in the tool's IPC namespace: visible when every port is held here and one proof port is announced by no other participant; not-visible when a port is absent here or is the tool's own; otherwise unprobed (always unprobed for the tool's own participants)

shm_ports.description: SHM unicast ports its endpoints announce, ros_discovery_info included; empty for a participant on another host

lock.description: the port's lock file (fastrtps_port<N>_el) in the tool's /dev/shm: held by a living process of this IPC namespace, the tool's own, absent, stale (nobody holds it), unknown (could not be probed) or unprobed (no scan)

announced_by.description: discovered participants announcing this port number, this one included

proof.description: false when only the participant's ros_discovery_info reader announces it: its 7000+ unique-flow number is the first free one of the IPC namespace in any domain, so a held lock does not prove whose it is
